title: Human evaluation: rubrics, sampling and inter-rater agreement

videos.script: A judge grades the traffic. Something has to grade the judge, and that is people. {{people}} Two people read the same forty-eight replies against one sentence: does the reply address the question. {{rubric}} They agree on two thirds of them. Chance alone would give exactly as much. Kappa, the agreement beyond chance, is zero. {{v1}} Every disagreement is a refusal. One read the sentence as about the question, the other as answering it. {{refusal}} So they wrote the answer into the rubric, with a real reply for every rule. Kappa rises to nearly zero point seven. {{v2}} Then the judge, against their agreed labels. It fails every refusal, and eleven good answers. {{judge}} Deciding refusals from the answer key doubles its kappa. Giving it the people's rubric makes it worse. {{rule}} Agreement flatters. Kappa says what the judge actually sees, and only labels can tell a better judge from a worse one. {{end}}
